doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: His strict father and the family's reaction to jazz
summary: His father wanted university and a job; after his mother died when Tanaka was 17 he softened.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Wow. Did your parents — what did they think of your fascination with jazz?

My father is a very strict person, you know, very down to earth. And you had to go to the university and find a job. My mother — my father always kind of had the upper hand. So I must follow whatever my father — my mother passed away when I was 17 years old. At that time my father’s friend said to him, “let your son do what he wants.” Especially this kind of vocation. You know my mother passed away. So then he asked me, “do you have anything to do?” And yea, okay good. Before that I told him I wanted to play music. “What for? How much money you can make? How is the insurance?”
No way. But after my mother passed away he kind of softened. And after that everything was fine.
It’s interesting, because I almost guessed that he would have got more strict with you.
